correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and strictly positive rates the exact cyclic resolvent diagonal is 1/((1+t r_i)(1-Π t r_j/(1+t r_j))). Its derivative has sign given by U(1+S)-1, where U=Π_{j!=i}z_j and S=Σ_{j!=i}(1-z_j); U<=exp(-S)<1/(1+S). Thus each return is strictly decreasing; common denominator makes maximum-rate states lowest. The limiting stationary mass of a maximum-rate state is <=1/n<1/2, so one positive root of the polynomial is the sole boundary. C=2R-I and strict positivity of off-diagonal R yield the if-and-only-if claim. Uniform-case strict size monotonicity and 2^(n-1)(x_n-1)->1 follow from the root equation and exponential bound. Exact-rational checker passed 6020 cases but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The general Cayley/resolvent diagonal test is explicitly credited; the new claim instead proves strict time monotonicity without reversibility for every inhomogeneous clockwise cycle, identifies the first failing states by maximum exit rate, obtains a sharp polynomial root, and determines an exponential uniform-size correction. Full claim/implication comparison with the closest general record found no theorem for these nonreversible cycle parameters. Published time-stepping and Dirichlet-grid papers studied distinct general schemes/undirected grids.

value.rationale: The fixed directed cycle with heterogeneous rates is a natural nonreversible transport and Markov discretization, where scalar A-stability does not guarantee nonnegative numerical states. A complete positivity frontier for arbitrary n and rates, the exact fast-exit bottleneck, and exponential finite-size correction provide relevant nontrivial structure and an directly computable criterion. The result extends the reversible-only crossing theory by a renewal-product argument, not a relabelled eigenvalue substitution.
